Based on the search results, here's what Claude Code Hooks are:

## Overview

Claude Code Hooks are shell commands that run automatically when specific events happen during your AI coding session. Think of hooks like git hooks, but for your AI agent.

## Key Purpose

A hook is a user-defined command (or HTTP endpoint, or MCP tool, or sub-model evaluation) that Claude Code executes deterministically at a fixed point in the tool-and-conversation lifecycle. The critical distinction is that hooks inject deterministic processing into Claude Code's lifecycle. Unlike prompt instructions, which are requests that Claude may interpret flexibly, hooks execute the same way every time.

## Common Use Cases

Claude Code hooks automate coding tasks like testing, formatting, and receiving notifications. You can set up hooks for code formatting, test execution, notifications, and file protection.

## How They Work

A hook starts with an event, can optionally be narrowed with a matcher, receives structured input from Claude Code, and then executes one or more handlers. Configure them in .claude/settings.json (project) or ~/.claude/settings.json (global) using JSON with events, matchers, and commands.

## Practical Advantage

The critical difference from prompt-based rules is that hooks are guaranteed to execute. If you set up a PreToolUse hook that blocks writes to .env files, it will always block them.
